v11.79 - x-94: bir misyona projenin ne olduğu söylenir, sırada ne olduğu değil

A person ran an adaptive objective, read the planner's transcript, and found
this project's BACKLOG in it — five unrelated items, the recent worklog, and an
instruction to record what it did in the worklog before finishing. None of that
is a mission's subject.

A mission arrives with an objective, its constraints and its success criteria.
The project's standing work is the question a SESSION opens with; the write-back
protocol is addressed to a person's own conversation, not to a headless delegate
that would then file worklog lines about work nobody asked it to record.

THE BRIEF NOW HAS AN AUDIENCE.

  · the mission copy keeps the MAP — what the project is, its people, its code
    roots, and which document holds which role. Deliberately: a mission CAN be
    told to record something, and then it has to know where.
  · it drops the four standing lists — open plan items, top of the backlog,
    recent decisions, recent worklog — and the session's write-back tail.
  · NOT MERELY HIDDEN. `briefSource` returns early for this audience, so a
    mission spawn does not read Plan.md, Backlog.md or Worklog.md at all. The
    test counts the reads rather than trusting the absence of the words.
  · the frame around it stops saying "work on this project" and "record what you
    did in the worklog", and says the objective is the work.
  · the lead's briefing says the omission OUT LOUD. It used to promise "what is
    open on it", which is now deliberately false — a briefing that goes on
    promising a list somebody removed sends the lead reading files for it.
  · two audiences, two files. A mission's delegations ARE spawns and they happen
    while somebody is starting a session; one path for both means whichever
    wrote last decides what the other reads. `_AF/BRIEF.md` stays the session
    document and a mission never rewrites it.

AND THE SECOND HALF OF THE SAME QUESTION — is a mission even associated with a
project? It was, invisibly. `MissionSpec.projectId` has existed since Faz 5 and
this form drew no control for it, so a mission started while the window sat on a
project was filed under it, briefed with it and had every delegation filed under
it, without the word "project" appearing anywhere on the form.

There is a Project box now, offering all three answers the host has always
accepted: this window's project (the visible default, named in the option), a
deliberate none, or one you pick. An untouched box posts the exact message it
posted before the control existed. `missions.preview` and the caption both say
WHICH of the two it was — `requested` or `window` — because "inherited while you
were not looking" is the answer to the question that opened this item.

The caption was wrong once and a rendered picture caught it: it read the preview
alone, so before the host answered it claimed "filed under no project" beneath a
box reading "this window's project: …". It is derived from the form now and the
host's reply overrides only when it exists.

Measured in test/test_project_audience.js (new, 50 assertions — including the
read count and the byte-identical session file name), test_mission_project.js
and test_missions_webview.js. Looked at: dist/render/missions.png, dark and
light. 13980 tests pass.
